$comment: Frozen byte-level conformance vectors for core#2070 (R15/D19). The identity value is SHA-256 over the pre-image encoded UTF-8, lowercase hex. A mismatch on preImage names the slot; a mismatch on identityKey alone means the hashing or encoding differs.

vectors.why: R16 material branch: `K:` is SHA-256 over the LOWERCASE HEX of the decoded bytes — not over the bytes, and not the target's identity key

R16 material branch TWO, the commonest real spelling: a PEM-armoured value is NOT decodable base64, so the digest is SHA-256 over the value VERBATIM — armour, newlines and all. An implementer given only branch one diverges on every armoured key
R16 algorithm branch: `A:` is the target algorithm's own identity, so it moves with the target's name and parameter set and NOT with its `primitive`
every algorithm slot populated at once, so slot ORDER is frozen

no derivable family: the normalized-name discriminator branch. OTR is deliberate -- it is corpus-witnessed, outside every table, and its defect-or-correct-answer ruling is still open, so it is a name this branch should keep answering for
three registry spellings of one curve fold to secg/*
an off-vocabulary residue that stays in the key (L7)
`other` is a real enum value, not a placeholder (D13)
D0's suffix: a stated capability rather than an observed deployment
no name and no family: the payload-digest backstop
the content-digest tier, from the 1.7 fingerprint field
the DN composite: type→OID, RDN sort, epoch timestamps

vectors.why: suite codes as unpadded bytes, joined in array order
the same suite comma-packed: must equal the unpadded vector

the same suite as a single whole two-byte code: must equal the unpadded and packed vectors. CycloneDX's own 1.7 conformance fixture spells TLS 1.3 suites this way, so a strict one-octet parser passes every other suite vector and still splits the fixture's rows off from the corpus'

a suite whose high byte is zero, packed: the rendered width must be the producer's own rounded up to an octet, not the width of the integer. Rendering the parsed value drops the leading zeros and yields `2f`, which both forks from the per-byte spelling below and collides with a malformed one-byte `["0x2F"]` -- and the whole classic TLS block, 0x002F/0x0035/0x000A, lives in this range. `0x1301` cannot witness this: its high byte is non-zero, so it renders identically either way
the same suite one element per byte: must equal the packed spelling above, which is the property the 0x0000-0x00FF range breaks when the width comes from the integer rather than the producer
the posture/endpoint slot, appended only when non-empty (D12)
the value-digest tier for a public key
a producer id containing the slot separator must not forge a tier
a password: identity uses the digest, the stored payload does not

a literal `%` in a keyed value escapes to `%25`, in ONE pass with the other escapes. No prior vector carried a literal `%`, so an implementation that never escapes it passed all 248 — and unescaped, an id containing the TEXT `%7C` forges the same key as an id containing a real `|`

prt:type+occurrence slot 3 holds the STABLE NAME, not the type, and the occurrence digest is appended to it. The tier's only prior vector was a component named `TLS` whose stable name is byte-identical to its type, so both readings produced the same bytes; this one settles it, and its two out-of-order occurrences also pin the sorted join

a `cryptographic-asset` with no `cryptoProperties` at all keys on the unroutable backstop WITH ITS NAME IN THE KEY: the projection digest of an absent properties object is identical for every such component, so without the name every broken asset in an estate collapses into one row — the over-merge §4.22 records, previously covered by zero vectors

an UNKNOWN `assetType` routes to the same unroutable backstop, never to a property chain — routing is on `assetType` alone. The normalizer folds an unrecognized type to None, so the assetType slot is empty and the projection digest (which still carries the raw string) plus the name discriminate

the type-only protocol tier: a type, no version, no suites, no usable name, no occurrences. Kernel-reachable and listed in no prior artifact — the atlas listed 21 of the kernel's 23 chain steps and its completeness assertion only covered steps the census or the vector set already knew
a protocol with no `type` at all falls to the protocol backstop: the canonical projection digest, keyed under RAW|protocol. The second of the two kernel tiers no artifact listed

D0's `|claimed` suffix is appended by the tier-independent tail of `identity()`, so it applies to EVERY asset type — the only prior claimed vector was an algorithm, so a reading that suffixes algorithms alone passed all 248

R16 material branch through the 1.7 spelling: the public key is named by `relatedCryptographicAssets[type=public-key].ref`, not by 1.6's `subjectPublicKeyRef`, and the entry type is matched separator-dropped and case-folded. Certificate, target and value are those of `crt-dn-public-key-target`, so the two spellings MUST land on one key -- a 1.6 producer and a 1.7 producer describing one certificate must not fork it. The entry type is spelled `PublicKey`, a real producer spelling, so that the fold is load-bearing: spelled canonically, a reader comparing the type raw reproduces this key and the vector proves nothing. A reader that compares the entry type raw, or reads the entry's `bom-ref` instead of its `ref`, resolves nothing and keys this certificate on an EMPTY `K:` slot

a serialNumber spelling the ratified sentinel `unknown` is an absent serial: keyed, it gave every certificate of the issuer one CRT|S row, so the pair falls to the distinguished-name composite. Curated 2026-09-04; the composite's inner pre-image is published so the slot is testable
